cases.payer: Time-poor Irish family with photos in iCloud, phone backups and old disks
cases.trigger: Inherited/accumulated photos across sources must be reliably consolidated without losing memories
cases.money_evidence: The Photo Gatherer (Dublin) advertises digital sorting from €1,000, with an alternative price page €995 up to 10k photos, €1,750 up to 25k, from €2,500 over 50k; UK Clear Bubble £960/£1,560/£2,040; named testimonials vendor-hosted, NO independent paid invoices
cases.complete_paid_outcome: One searchable deduplicated and chronologically organized original-preserving photo/video archive, handed back with tested backup plan and no missing photos
cases.convenience_vs_nonsoftware: Much of charge covers 20–40 hours gathering files, safely interpreting near-duplicates/missing EXIF/people events, guiding low-technical clients and backup reassurance; portions mechanisable
cases.input_output: Customer-supplied exports from iCloud/Google Photos/phones/USBs -> immutable manifest, verified reorganized full-resolution originals, reversible duplicate review and 3-2-1 backup evidence
cases.verification: Checksums per original, duplicate SHA/perceptual candidate groups, EXIF provenance and sample restore checks verify bytes and backup; significance of near duplicates, missing timestamp, Live Photos and external cloud exports need human choices
cases.competitors: Mylio Photos+ from $25/mo, Apple's and Google's photo products, Immich self-hosted, PhotoMove/duplicate utilities
cases.repeat_ai: An AI assistant can suggest folder/event grouping, but cannot safely operate 100k mixed formats and reversible cloud exports with zero risk via chat
cases.ai_build: A local desktop application with importer, hash manifest and 3-2-1 backup integration is feasible; difficult UX/onboarding/trust and ordinary professional customer's refusal to perform DIY are severe
cases.recurrence_first_ten: High per-household one-off price, potentially many families; Irish firms exist but no ten independently verified customers willing to buy DIY instead of a done-for-you migration; service's own names do not prove paid purchase
cases.strongest_kill: The full €1k purchase is **personal operation and reassurance**, while commercial substitute Mylio already automates much at $25/mo; customer file custody/storage and support would be unusually onerous
cases.cheapest_falsification: Find 3 independently interviewed Irish families who paid >=€750 for **digital-only** organising (no print/scanning), and ask whether they would have opted for self-service under €250 and what prevented them. Before a build demonstrate reversible 10-source archive test and restoration integrity.

cases.payer: UK time-poor household professional with disorganised OneDrive/Dropbox/Google Drive
cases.trigger: Old personal digital files and folders need consolidated naming and structure
cases.money_evidence: UK virtual assistant advertises a fixed one-off cloud storage organisation package from £105, no confirmed paid transactions
cases.complete_paid_outcome: Old personal docs refiled to an agreed folder taxonomy with useful names and accessible paths
cases.convenience_vs_nonsoftware: Paying for consultant to choose meaningful household taxonomy and deal with unique exceptions, rather than programmatic name sorting alone
cases.input_output: User cloud drive export or permitted account -> renamed, classified non-destructive folder structure and mapping log
cases.verification: Counts/hashes and rollback auditable, meaningful personal categories and correct privacy/storage permissions require review
cases.competitors: Google Drive/OneDrive search and labels, Windows Power Automate, file renamers
cases.repeat_ai: General AI can classify batches of named PDFs reasonably but misfiles ambiguous legal/personal docs, and unsafe share/permissions risky
cases.ai_build: AI agent or local rule-based classifier straightforward; metadata and account permissions complicated with low £105 one-off price
cases.recurrence_first_ten: UK home organisation buyers identifiable, but no verified 10 buyers pay to have a software agent separate from ordinary files apps
cases.strongest_kill: Fee too small to support onboarding, cloud OAuth and trust/recovery liability; recurring use absent
cases.cheapest_falsification: No revival without bulk repeat operator or provider-side paid licensed workflow evidence

cases.payer: UK owner of an obsolete appliance needing functioning replacement
cases.trigger: Broken discontinued clip/hinge has no downloadable STL and original replacement is unavailable
cases.money_evidence: UK CAD/3D-print design seller explicitly prices exact-fit custom replacement CAD £140–£300 for 1–2 weeks, with STEP and STL rights; price advert not paid invoice
cases.complete_paid_outcome: Dimensionally correct parametric CAD replacement part plus manufacturable STL / STEP, distinct from a physical printed item
cases.convenience_vs_nonsoftware: Convenience is paying engineer to reverse-model fit and tolerance from damaged/partial physical part; client often owns only photos and rough measurements
cases.input_output: Photos with ruler + critical dimensions -> correctly engineered, print-tested editable part file (physical prototype optional)
cases.verification: STL manifold/fit envelope and CAD measurement checks available, but hidden snap-fit strain/clearance/part function cannot be verified from incomplete photos
cases.competitors: CAD designers, Fusion 360, free Printables/Thingiverse models, photo-to-3D AI
cases.repeat_ai: AI image-to-3D readily creates rough shape but cannot infer hidden tolerances and functional stress reliably without testing
cases.ai_build: AI-built mesh generator possible, end-to-end functional part requires physical prototyping and a mechanical engineer for each variant
cases.recurrence_first_ten: Bespoke one-off from homeowners, weak repeated lifetime volume and no evidence customers prefer automated output to accountable maker
cases.strongest_kill: Complete paid value is expert functional part engineering; output exactness critical and high error rate likely
cases.cheapest_falsification: No project absent known dimensional drawing/accepted model; a niche fixed-part library would be a different business

cases.payer: UK genealogy enthusiast preparing tree export for family sharing
cases.trigger: GEDCOM import produces duplicate relatives, impossible dates and broken family links
cases.money_evidence: UK established file-check-and-correct service sells £40 for 1–500 individuals, £50 for 501–999, £60 for 1000–1500, with caveat work time and extra approvals
cases.complete_paid_outcome: Clean GEDCOM file with structural repairs, preserved identities and annotated uncertain errors
cases.convenience_vs_nonsoftware: Fee buys human judgment on whether records refer to same person and how to mend a family tree, not mechanical file validation
cases.input_output: GEDCOM -> validated identity-safe tree with changed-record audit and unchanged original
cases.verification: GEDCOM format/links/date invariants machine-checkable, but genuine duplicate person resolution needs record evidence
cases.competitors: Free in-browser GEDCOM checker and many genealogy software tools
cases.repeat_ai: AI can suggest duplicate resolution but mixes similarly named relatives, creating irreparable canonical ancestry errors
cases.ai_build: Parser/validator is straightforward, existing free validators already find 31+ kinds of issues; any further corrections require research judgment
cases.recurrence_first_ten: Genealogy associations accessible, price too low and repeat business weak
cases.strongest_kill: Automatable validation already free, sensitive relationship truth and error liability remain human; routine output cannot capture full £40 correction service
cases.cheapest_falsification: No automated account of true family identity with authoritative ground truth

cases.payer: UK amateur documentarian / traveller illustrating a route in a video
cases.trigger: Need a finished location-accurate animated journey map with effects from itinerary
cases.money_evidence: Fiverr buyer in UK reports $50–$100 paid range on a related Google map animation gig; original specialist has 88 reviews and multiple $50 transactions by overseas buyers; no recurring UK spend evidenced
cases.complete_paid_outcome: Approved route-driven animated 1080p/4K footage with pins, camera moves and labelled landmarks
cases.convenience_vs_nonsoftware: Buyer actually buys independent digital animation instead of manually keyframing; creative camera choreography and polish included, but no explicit urgency guarantee
cases.input_output: User route waypoints and location labels -> rendered clean animation with geography and licensed map asset use
cases.verification: Coordinate consistency/duration/video codec checkable; cinematic style/licensing/visual preferences subjective
cases.competitors: Google Earth Studio, After Effects templates, inexpensive Fiverr gig from $5; map-animation web apps
cases.repeat_ai: General AI and map-animation templates can create quick route visuals repeatedly but geography correctness still needs validation
cases.ai_build: Animation app technically feasible but commoditized, map tile imagery/licensing issues and one-off $50 order economics
cases.recurrence_first_ten: UK hobby filmmakers reachable in creator networks, first-ten paid interest and meaningful recurrence unproved
cases.strongest_kill: Ticket price too small and creative revisions compete with cheap specialists/ready tools; earlier travel itinerary kill is a different purchased job, but similar commercialization weakness
cases.cheapest_falsification: No subscription-worthy recurring customer and positive buyer selection versus free templates
